CALL.meaning: Incoming remote call at the receiving component.
CALL.enabledBy: Event filter and property all; filters only reduce generated data.
CALL.keyProperties: Context, Func, CallID, ClientID, t:clientID, SessionID, t:connectID, Usr; CpuTime in us; Memory/MemoryPeak in bytes; InBytes/OutBytes are disk I/O.
CALL.badSigns: Large duration, CPU, memory peak or many repetitions.
CALL.traps: Nested calls overlap: do not sum them as independent work. A CALL is not necessarily one user action.
CALL.fixes: Locate the expensive component and repeat the same scenario.
CALL.cost: High event volume is possible; measure this profile on the target workload.

SCALL.meaning: Outgoing remote call; the destination need not be a DBMS.
SCALL.enabledBy: Event filter and property all; filters only reduce generated data.
SCALL.keyProperties: CallID, ClientID, DstClientID, IName, MName, Interface, Method, Context.
SCALL.badSigns: Long receiver wait or many short calls.
SCALL.traps: [unverified] SCALL minus CALL duration is not proven pure network time; pair identities and boundaries first.
SCALL.fixes: Batch repeated calls; inspect the receiver.
SCALL.cost: High event volume is possible; measure this profile on the target workload.

SDBL.meaning: Platform data-model operation, including queries and transaction boundaries.
SDBL.enabledBy: Event filter and property all; filters only reduce generated data.
SDBL.keyProperties: Func, Sdbl (platform data-model query text), Context; BeginTransaction, CommitTransaction, RollbackTransaction.
SDBL.traps: HoldConnection and transaction events are not individual SQL statements. SDBL and child DB durations overlap.
SDBL.fixes: Inspect SQL, transaction scope and unexplained platform time.
SDBL.cost: High event volume is possible; measure this profile on the target workload.

DBMSSQL.enabledBy: Event filter and property all; filters only reduce generated data.
DBMSSQL.keyProperties: Sql, Context, dbpid, Rows, RowsAffected, planSQLText; plans require plansql; lock annotations require dbmslocks.
DBMSSQL.badSigns: High count, total, max duration; expensive plan or waits.
DBMSSQL.traps: RowsAffected=-1 is not a negative row count. Decode physical names using the actual database structure. Duration alone does not distinguish CPU, I/O and blocking.
DBMSSQL.fixes: Inspect BSL context, data volumes, plan, statistics and waits before changing indexes.
DBMSSQL.cost: High event volume is possible; measure this profile on the target workload.

DBPOSTGRS.enabledBy: Event filter and property all; filters only reduce generated data.
DBPOSTGRS.keyProperties: Sql, Context, dbpid, Rows, RowsAffected, planSQLText; plans require plansql; lock annotations require dbmslocks.
DBPOSTGRS.badSigns: High count, total, max duration; expensive plan or waits.
DBPOSTGRS.traps: Plan cost is not seconds. actual time is ms; rows and time are per loop. Estimated plans are not actual execution. Duration alone does not distinguish CPU, I/O and blocking.
DBPOSTGRS.fixes: Inspect BSL context, data volumes, plan, statistics and waits before changing indexes.
DBPOSTGRS.cost: High event volume is possible; measure this profile on the target workload.

DBV8DBENG.enabledBy: Event filter and property all; filters only reduce generated data.
DBV8DBENG.keyProperties: Sql, Context, dbpid, Rows, RowsAffected, planSQLText; plans require plansql; lock annotations require dbmslocks.
DBV8DBENG.badSigns: High count, total, max duration; expensive plan or waits.
DBV8DBENG.traps: Use file-engine plan notation (FULL SCAN, USING INDEX, NESTED LOOP), not PostgreSQL/SQL Server rules. Duration alone does not distinguish CPU, I/O and blocking.
DBV8DBENG.fixes: Inspect BSL context, data volumes, plan, statistics and waits before changing indexes.
DBV8DBENG.cost: High event volume is possible; measure this profile on the target workload.

TLOCK.meaning: Managed transactional lock acquisition, including wait time.
TLOCK.enabledBy: Event filter and property all; filters only reduce generated data.
TLOCK.badSigns: Nonempty WaitConnections or repeated long waits.
TLOCK.traps: Acquisition duration is not holding lifetime; a region name alone does not prove a whole-register lock. dbmslocks is not required.
TLOCK.fixes: Collect short acquisitions and transaction boundaries; check resource intersections and access order.
TLOCK.cost: High event volume is possible; measure this profile on the target workload.

TTIMEOUT.enabledBy: Event filter and property all; filters only reduce generated data.
TTIMEOUT.traps: Duration may be zero; use the associated TLOCK wait. Victim context does not identify the holder.
TTIMEOUT.fixes: Collect the locks profile on all participants; shorten the proven conflicting transaction.
TTIMEOUT.cost: Incident/lifecycle volume is usually lower, but storms can be large; no fixed guarantee.

TDEADLOCK.enabledBy: Event filter and property all; filters only reduce generated data.
TDEADLOCK.keyProperties: DeadlockConnectionIntersections, Context; correlate TLOCK and transactions.
TDEADLOCK.badSigns: Any occurrence; repeated contexts suggest a reproducible access-order issue.
TDEADLOCK.traps: Not a universal DBMS deadlock event; zero duration is not harmless.
TDEADLOCK.fixes: Align resource order and modes; reproduce concurrently and check timeouts and waits too.
TDEADLOCK.cost: Incident/lifecycle volume is usually lower, but storms can be large; no fixed guarantee.

EXCP.meaning: Exception in platform, application, network or DBMS.
EXCP.enabledBy: Event filter and property all; filters only reduce generated data.
EXCP.keyProperties: Exception, Descr, Context, OSException, DumpFile; retain the whole cause chain.
EXCP.badSigns: New repeated errors near failed operations or process loss.
EXCP.traps: One business failure can produce multiple component events. [article: Infobot / Infostart] EXCP outside expected filters was observed; [unverified] not a universal contract.
EXCP.fixes: Fix the evidenced defect; preserve version, reproduction and dump for unexplained crashes.
EXCP.cost: Incident/lifecycle volume is usually lower, but storms can be large; no fixed guarantee.

EXCPCNTX.meaning: Snapshot of operations started but unfinished at an abnormal condition.
EXCPCNTX.enabledBy: Event filter and property all; filters only reduce generated data.
EXCPCNTX.keyProperties: SrcName is the original operation; events are emitted from deepest nesting outward.
EXCPCNTX.traps: A filter alone does not generate snapshots. [unverified] Exclude snapshots from successful operation totals to avoid double counting.
EXCPCNTX.fixes: Inspect the original exception and interrupted stack.
EXCPCNTX.cost: Incident/lifecycle volume is usually lower, but storms can be large; no fixed guarantee.

QERR.meaning: Query compilation, row/field access restriction or optional external-source NULL validation error.
QERR.enabledBy: Event filter and property all; filters only reduce generated data.
QERR.badSigns: Repeated errors at the same application location or permissions.
QERR.traps: Query is not DBMS SQL. Additional NULL validation can substantially slow queries.
QERR.fixes: Inspect query syntax, permissions and data; query checkActualNullable=true enables special NULL checking.
QERR.cost: Incident/lifecycle volume is usually lower, but storms can be large; no fixed guarantee.

PROC.enabledBy: Event filter and property all; filters only reduce generated data.
PROC.keyProperties: process, PID, Func and lifecycle description.
PROC.badSigns: Explicit abnormal termination; unexplained frequent turnover needs corroboration.
PROC.traps: Normal starts/stops and configured restarts are not crashes. Infrastructure-specific process-count advice is not a universal alert.
PROC.fixes: Correlate exceptions, monitoring, version and process dumps.
PROC.cost: Incident/lifecycle volume is usually lower, but storms can be large; no fixed guarantee.

CONN.enabledBy: Event filter and property all; filters only reduce generated data.
CONN.keyProperties: Action, client, application, addresses, connection identifiers.
CONN.badSigns: Many reconnects near a component failure.
CONN.traps: Session, client connection and DBMS connection are different identities.
CONN.cost: Incident/lifecycle volume is usually lower, but storms can be large; no fixed guarantee.

SESN.enabledBy: Event filter and property all; filters only reduce generated data.
SESN.badSigns: [unverified] Unusual actions or repeated recovery warrant correlation.
SESN.traps: A session can outlive a connection; SessionID may be absent on an unassigned thread.
SESN.fixes: Check CONN, PROC, EXCP and actual job/session history.
SESN.cost: Incident/lifecycle volume is usually lower, but storms can be large; no fixed guarantee.

MEM.meaning: Growth of unfreed dynamic memory fragments between suitable idle checkpoints.
MEM.enabledBy: Event filter and property all; filters only reduce generated data.
MEM.keyProperties: sz size, szd delta, cn fragment count, cnd count delta.
MEM.traps: Not periodic RSS; generation depends on no active calls/jobs. Absence does not prove no growth.
MEM.fixes: Compare the same process before/after; inspect retained objects and dumps.

LEAKS.meaning: Tracked objects retained between checkpoints, with creation stacks.
LEAKS.enabledBy: Event filter and property all; filters only reduce generated data.
LEAKS.keyProperties: Descr contains object types and creation stacks.
LEAKS.badSigns: [unverified] Repeatable accumulation after the measured section.
LEAKS.traps: Retained objects may be intentional; this does not detect all native leaks.
LEAKS.fixes: Narrow checkpoint to the implicated procedure and inspect lifetime.
LEAKS.cost: Adds overhead; narrow to a procedure after localization.

ATTN.enabledBy: Event filter and property all; filters only reduce generated data.
ATTN.keyProperties: Text/type, PID, MemSize, MaxMemSize, MemoryLimits when available.
ATTN.badSigns: Unavailable process or critical memory limit.
ATTN.traps: A failure notification may only report a downstream symptom.
ATTN.fixes: Correlate component log and OS resource measurements.
ATTN.cost: Incident/lifecycle volume is usually lower, but storms can be large; no fixed guarantee.

CLSTR.enabledBy: Event filter and property all; filters only reduce generated data.
CLSTR.keyProperties: Event, Data; performance update metrics depend on version.
CLSTR.badSigns: Load imbalance or repeated moves need investigation.
CLSTR.traps: Not every CLSTR event is an error; Data has multiple shapes.
CLSTR.fixes: Inspect cluster settings and measured resource constraints.
CLSTR.cost: Incident/lifecycle volume is usually lower, but storms can be large; no fixed guarantee.

SDGC.enabledBy: Event filter and property all; filters only reduce generated data.

SDGC.badSigns: Growth and maintenance waits coinciding with complaints.
SDGC.traps: Not general BSL memory garbage collection.
SDGC.fixes: Use sessiondatacontext to investigate session-data origins only when needed; it adds overhead.
SDGC.cost: Incident/lifecycle volume is usually lower, but storms can be large; no fixed guarantee.

VRSREQUEST.enabledBy: Event filter and property all; filters only reduce generated data.
VRSREQUEST.keyProperties: URI, Method, Headers, Body (body size in bytes), vrs-session, sync.
VRSREQUEST.traps: VRS is not a whole business-action measurement and can differ by connection mode. [unverified] Generality across modes is not established. CALL InBytes/OutBytes are disk I/O.
VRSREQUEST.fixes: Measure the whole user operation before form opening; reduce unnecessary form data; use WPR/WPA or network tools for unexplained time.
VRSREQUEST.cost: High event volume is possible; measure this profile on the target workload.

VRSRESPONSE.fixes: Measure the whole user operation before form opening; reduce unnecessary form data; use WPR/WPA or network tools for unexplained time.

generation.note: Event/property filters only reduce output. MEM needs mem; LEAKS needs leaks and checkpoints; plans need plansql; DBMS lock annotations need dbmslocks.

plans-disagreement.note: [doc] PostgreSQL methodology restricts plansql to test/development servers. [article: Dmitry Yukhtimovsky] and [article: Nikolay Kuznetsov] older profiles collect plans with slow SQL. Preserve both recommendations and dates (2017 / 2024-2026); do not call plans cheap permanent monitoring.

units-disagreement.note: [article: badcasedaily / OTUS] uses Dur; not documented as equivalent to duration/durationus. [article: Konstmax13] corrected filter units on 2026-10-23. Generate durationus, never Dur. [doc] Historical 8.1 used ten-thousandths of a second; exact transition remains [unverified].

invalid-examples.note: [article: Nikolay Kuznetsov] includes a leading space in SDBL and system nested under log. Documented token is SDBL; system belongs under config.

disk-not-network.note: CALL InBytes/OutBytes are disk I/O despite contrary article interpretations. VRS Body is exchange data.

absence.note: Absent does not mean healthy: disabled event, duration filtering, generation settings, missing node, active unfinished call and version can all explain absence.

identities.note: [unverified] Correlation must scope node, process, infobase and interval. Equal numbers across SessionID, t:connectID, ClientID and dbpid do not link identities.

nested-time.note: [unverified] Use union of child intervals for residual time; summing nested durations double counts. Residual time is unexplained by captured events, not proven BSL CPU.

ibsrv.note: [article: Autumn Library] observed file-mode code without CALL and ibsrv CALL depth 0 without t:clientID on macOS 8.3.27. Generality on Windows/Linux and other releases is [unverified]. Never assume only rphost directories.

file-lock-matrix.note: [unverified] No sufficient basis for asserting TLOCK/TTIMEOUT/TDEADLOCK never occur in every file, web and ibsrv mode. Verify each mode/version.

cost.note: No universal MB/day, negligible-overhead, memory, row or process-count thresholds are established. Filters reduce recorded volume, not necessarily instrumentation cost. More than 20 log elements is discouraged.

retention.note: history is hours; 0 disables automatic deletion, not logging. rotationsize is MB per file, not a total directory cap. Gilev short 2-hour, IBS week and analytic long-retention advice serve different tasks.

versions.note: JSON/placement/new rotation arrived in 8.3.25. CALL memory/I/O expanded in 8.3.5; CpuTime in 8.3.13. 8.5.1 filter-unit confirmation does not prove every property unchanged.

source-access.note: ITS lock and deadlock methodologies were available as indexed excerpts (direct 403); gilev.ru pages via index (redirect loops); Burmistrov via index (429); PGConf PDF text only, XML images not transcribed. Books and 2012 attachments were not read; no claims from their unseen contents.

json-unknowns.note: [unverified] Duplicate keys and malformed property names need real-corpus verification. This parser rejects duplicate case-insensitive keys rather than repairing semantics. Unknown event kinds remain readable.

causality.note: [unverified] Keep fact, diagnostic hypothesis, missing evidence and recommendation separate. lka/lkp proves observed blocking, not a deadlock cycle. Carrier event may not be the resource-acquiring SQL.

service-account.note: A service-account cluster does not read the interactive user LOCALAPPDATA. Configuration lookup: version bin/conf, user LOCALAPPDATA/1C/1cv8/conf, ConfLocation, ALLUSERSPROFILE/1C/1cv8/conf. Earlier files shadow later ones.

capture-window.note: Scenario is a short manual bounded reproduction: start, reproduce once, stop immediately; history is retention, not automatic capture expiry.

plans-execution.note: EXPLAIN ANALYZE really executes SQL. Do not automatically replay data-changing statements. Reproduce platform connection settings; historic SET lists are not current universal defaults.

instrumentation.note: mem, leaks, scriptcircrefs, query NULL validation and sessiondatacontext add overhead. Full Windows dumps can be large; history does not delete dumps. Linux/macOS dumps use OS facilities.

methodology-scope.note: [doc] Classify whether the slowdown affects all users, one user, the whole system or one function; reproduce on comparable problem-user data. PostgreSQL methodology uses DB time share around 50 percent as a reason to inspect SQL, not a universal failure boundary. [unverified] Nested interval overlap must be removed before interpreting ratios. Use full-user-operation timing, including form serialization/client work outside the BSL timer.

log.meaning: JSON/plain dedicated location, retention hours and size rotation MB.
log.reason: Separate capture ownership and JSON parser compatibility.
log.cost: Size rotation does not cap total disk usage.

event.meaning: OR between event branches, AND between predicates in a branch.
event.reason: Collect selected profile events; filters only reduce generated data.
event.cost: Volume depends on event frequency; no fixed overhead guarantee.

property.meaning: all retains available context and correlation properties.
property.reason: Preserve evidence for details and chains.
property.cost: Larger records; diagnostic values can be sensitive.

durationus.reason: Reduce recorded long-call/DB volume; keep errors and locks unfiltered.
durationus.cost: Short parents and aggregate cost of short DB calls can be hidden.

infobase.meaning: Exact p:processName filter on every branch.
infobase.reason: Restrict a server capture to the requested infobase.
infobase.cost: Excludes client/file events lacking that property.

plansql.cost: [doc] PostgreSQL methodology: test/development only. Older articles differ; plan generation can be expensive even with output filters.

dbmslocks.cost: Extra DBMS queries no more often than once every 2 seconds on DB access; not a complete deadlock graph.

mem.reason: Memory profile or requested MEM event.

leaks.meaning: Track retained objects at server point checkpoints.
leaks.reason: Memory profile or requested LEAKS event.
leaks.cost: Adds overhead; narrow to a procedure after localization.

scriptcircrefs.cost: Substantial performance loss; focused diagnostics only.
